strengths: Principled and practical architectural design: The asymmetric encoder-decoder formulation effectively extends dual-path time-frequency sequence modeling to decouple input and output sampling rates (fE -> fD). Using learnable extension queries with a cross-self attention mechanism avoids redundant up/down-sampling computations.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The proposed system is rigorously evaluated across multiple benchmarks covering distinct settings: universal restoration (UNIVERSE), pure denoising (VCTK-DEMAND), multi-rate super-resolution under clean and corrupted conditions (VCTK), and real-world corrupted speech (VoxCeleb).

Effective training objectives: The proposed scaled log-spectral loss addresses the fundamental trade-off between oversmoothing and gradient explosion in complex spectral mapping, and the shared SFI-STFT discriminator enables stable adversarial training across multiple target sampling rates.
Streaming support and efficiency: The incorporation of Mamba into the time module enables a low-RTF streaming variant without substantial drops in restoration fidelity.

Clear ablation studies: The ablations convincingly demonstrate the importance of the scaled log-spectral loss over standard magnitude/complex L1 losses, the cross-self decoder structure, and the frequency projection inductive bias.
weaknesses: Lack of human subjective listening tests: All evaluations rely entirely on objective intrusive metrics (PESQ, SDR, LSD, MCD) and deep learning-based non-intrusive MOS predictors (UTMOS, WVMOS, DNSMOS). Because neural MOS estimators are known to be susceptible to adversarial and generative artifacts, human listening tests (e.g., MUSHRA or MOS ITU-T P.800) are needed to definitively validate perceptual quality.

Simulation bias in super-resolution evaluation: As acknowledged in Section 5.1, the noisy-distorted test set for super-resolution follows a degradation simulation pipeline very similar to the training pipeline, which may bias the comparison in favor of TF-Restormer over baselines.

Algorithmic latency in streaming mode: While computationally fast (low RTF), the streaming variant exhibits an algorithmic lookahead/latency of 80 ms (due to the 40 ms window, 20 ms hop, and non-causal 2D convolution layers), which is relatively high for strict real-time telecommunication scenarios that typically target latency under 20–40 ms.

High computational complexity (MACs): As reported in Table 6, dual-path sequence modeling incurs substantial Multiply-Accumulate operations (e.g., 240–518 GMACs per second of audio). While parallel execution on modern GPUs (RTX 4090) yields low RTF, this computational footprint could hinder deployment on edge or mobile devices.

strengths: The paper presents a well-motivated and elegant asymmetric encoder-decoder formulation based on sampling-frequency-independent STFT (SFI-STFT). Decoupling the input bandwidth analysis from the output bandwidth synthesis via learnable high-frequency extension queries effectively eliminates the need for redundant pre- or post-resampling.

Comprehensive architectural design: the introduction of a projection-based structural inductive bias in the frequency self-attention module stabilizes restoration, while replacing the temporal module with Mamba provides a practical low-latency causal streaming variant.
The proposed scaled log-spectral loss is mathematically well-analyzed (Figure 5) and intuitively addresses oversmoothing and gradient instability under severe distortions.

Extensive empirical evaluation covering multiple benchmarks: universal speech restoration (UNIVERSE), speech denoising (VCTK-DEMAND), super-resolution across diverse arbitrary sampling-rate pairs (8k/16k to 16k/24k/44.1k/48k), and real-world evaluation (VoxCeleb).
Thorough ablation studies verifying each core design choice: the scaled log-spectral loss, decoder structure with cross-attention (MHCA), and the frequency projection inductive bias.
weaknesses: Subjective human listening tests (e.g., MUSHRA or subjective MOS) are missing. While the evaluation includes a wide range of objective metrics (PESQ, SDR, LSD, MCD) and deep-learning-based non-intrusive MOS estimators (UTMOS, WVMOS, DNSMOS), neural perceptual quality estimators can exhibit known biases toward specific model architectures.

The model training is restricted to clean English speech sources from VCTK (98 speakers). As acknowledged in the limitations, synthetic degradation pipelines on studio recordings may limit out-of-domain robustness across diverse global accents, non-English languages, and complex real acoustic environments.

Although the measured Real-Time Factor (RTF) on an RTX 4090 is low, the raw MAC count of the dual-path architecture remains relatively high (e.g., 440-518 GMACs for 1-second speech), which could constrain deployment on resource-constrained edge hardware.

strengths: Decoupled SFI Input-Output Formulation: The use of a constant frame duration STFT (SFI-STFT) combined with an asymmetric encoder-decoder that operates on input bandwidth and expands frequencies via learnable extension queries is a well-motivated, practical solution to avoid redundant resampling and handle arbitrary input-output rates within a single model.

Comprehensive Empirical Benchmarking: The paper evaluates across several distinct restoration tasks—general multi-distortion restoration (UNIVERSE), denoising (VCTK-DEMAND), multi-rate super-resolution (8->16k, 8->24k, 8->44.1k, 16->48k), and real-world audio (VoxCeleb)—demonstrating consistent competitive performance against specialized and general baselines.

Streaming Feasibility with Mamba: Demonstrating that the time module of the TF dual-path network can be replaced with causal selective state spaces (Mamba) allows the system to achieve an 80 ms algorithmic latency and fast inference while retaining solid restoration quality.

Thorough Ablation Studies: Section 5.3 and Appendix E clearly justify the proposed architectural and loss choices, including the scaled log-spectral loss, the MHCA query decoder design, and the frequency projection structural bias.
weaknesses: Evaluation Bias from Training on Metric Predictors: Equation 6 explicitly includes human-feedback loss based on differentiable PESQ and UTMOS (\(L_{hf} = L_{pesq} + 10 \cdot L_{utmos}\)). Evaluating primarily with non-intrusive neural MOS estimators (UTMOS, WVMOS) and PESQ creates a significant optimization bias, making these automatic metrics less reliable without subjective human listening tests (e.g., MUSHRA or MOS).

Missing Anonymous Links for Code and Audio Demos: The manuscript references anonymous code and demo pages in both the Abstract and the Reproducibility Statement, but the actual URLs or identifiers are left blank, preventing verification of perceptual audio quality and reproducibility.

Incremental Architectural Novelty: The core components—TF dual-path modeling, SFI-STFT, Linformer-style projections, cross-self attention queries inspired by MAE, and Mamba for sequence modeling—are largely adapted from prior works (e.g., TF-Locoformer, Linformer, Siamese MAE), making the contribution more an engineering integration than a fundamentally new modeling paradigm.

Test Set Alignment for Super-Resolution: In Section 5.1 and Appendix D, the authors acknowledge that the synthetic evaluation for noisy-distorted super-resolution follows a degradation simulation pipeline very similar to the training pipeline, which may confer an artificial advantage over baselines.

strengths: Compelling problem formulation: Decoupling input and output sampling rates without requiring external resampling addresses a prominent bottleneck in speech restoration and audio super-resolution.

Well-motivated asymmetric architecture: Concentrating computational burden on the observed input bandwidth via a dual-path TF-encoder while synthesizing missing higher bands with a lightweight cross-attention query decoder is conceptually sound, efficient, and well-executed.

Methodological completeness: The paper introduces several synergistic components, including sampling-frequency-independent (SFI) STFT processing, a shared SFI-STFT discriminator, a projection-based frequency inductive bias, a causal Mamba variant for streaming, and an adaptive scaled log-spectral loss.

Thorough empirical evaluation: The proposed system is tested across diverse tasks and benchmarks (UNIVERSE GSR, VCTK-DEMAND denoising, multi-rate super-resolution, VoxCeleb, URGENT 2025, and DNS Challenge), demonstrating strong generalization across both clean and heavily distorted conditions.

Comprehensive and informative ablation studies: Ablations systematically isolate the value of the asymmetric encoder-decoder structure, cross-attention mechanism, shared frequency projection, loss function design, and sampling-rate training distributions.
weaknesses: Reliance on neural proxy metrics: The evaluation depends primarily on non-intrusive neural estimators (DNSMOS, UTMOS, NISQA) and objective metrics. Given that generative restoration models frequently exploit neural metric biases, a formal subjective listening test (e.g., MUSHRA or crowd-sourced subjective MOS) would provide more definitive validation.

Inherent trade-off on intrusive fidelity: As seen in the URGENT 2025 and DNS benchmarks, the universal model lags behind specialized discriminative enhancers in intrusive fidelity metrics (PESQ, SI-SDR), which is typical of generative setups but limits performance in purely deterministic enhancement scenarios.

WavLM perceptual loss bandwidth constraint: The self-supervised perceptual loss operates at 16 kHz, leaving higher frequencies (>8 kHz) dependent entirely on the scaled log-spectral and adversarial objectives, which may restrict acoustic naturalness at high target rates (44.1/48 kHz).

Computational load on edge devices: Although RTF on a high-end desktop GPU (RTX 4090) is low due to parallelism, the raw MAC count (up to 518 G MACs/s for 16->48 kHz) remains relatively heavy for low-power edge or mobile deployment.

strengths: Novel and practical problem formulation: The paper effectively addresses the decoupled input-output sampling rate problem ($f_E \to f_D$) in speech restoration without relying on external resampling, solving an important practical constraint in audio processing.

Well-motivated asymmetric query-based architecture: By restricting heavy TF-dual-path modeling to the observed input bandwidth in the encoder and delegating high-frequency synthesis to a lightweight cross-attention decoder with learnable extension queries sliced from a unified master prior, the model achieves computational efficiency and rate-invariant representations.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The proposed method is evaluated across a broad spectrum of restoration tasks, including general speech restoration (UNIVERSE), denoising (VCTK-DEMAND), speech super-resolution (VCTK), real-world data (VoxCeleb), and the competitive URGENT 2025 benchmark, demonstrating consistent performance in both offline and streaming (Mamba-based) settings.

Thorough and insightful ablation studies: The ablations convincingly demonstrate the necessity of the asymmetric encoder-decoder structure (compared against size-matched and computation-matched encoder-only baselines), the frequency-projection inductive bias, the unified SFI-STFT discriminator, and the proposed adaptive scaled log-spectral loss.

Transparent discussion of trade-offs: The authors provide an honest and rigorous analysis regarding the trade-offs between signal fidelity (intrusive metrics like PESQ/SDR) and perceptual naturalness (MOS estimators), as well as sensitivity to sampling-rate training distributions.
weaknesses: Reliance on neural perceptual metrics: The perceptual evaluations in the main paper primarily rely on automated neural estimators (UTMOS, DNSMOS, NISQA) rather than formal subjective listening tests (e.g., MUSHRA or crowd-sourced human MOS). While standard in recent literature, human verification would strengthen the claims regarding perceptual quality.

High multiply-accumulate complexity (MACs): Despite achieving low real-time factors (RTF) on a high-end GPU (RTX 4090), the raw computational cost remains substantial (200–500 GMACs/s), which may pose deployment challenges on edge devices or low-power CPUs.

Distributional overlap in synthetic SSR evaluation: As acknowledged in Section 5.1, the degradation pipeline for the synthetic test data closely mirrors the training simulation pipeline, which may confer a favorable inductive bias on the SSR benchmarks.

strengths: Novel and elegant decoupled formulation: Framing speech restoration and bandwidth extension under arbitrary input-output sampling rates within a single model—without requiring manual input/output resampling—addresses a long-standing constraint in the literature.

Well-motivated asymmetric architecture: Concentrating computational burden on the observed input spectrum via a TF dual-path encoder and generating missing spectral content via learnable frequency extension queries in a lightweight decoder offers both conceptual clarity and computational efficiency (lowering MACs and RTF when the input bandwidth is low).

Effective training objectives and discriminator design: The proposed adaptive scaled log-spectral loss effectively mitigates the gradient explosion and oversmoothing issues typical of missing high bands, while the shared SFI-STFT discriminator unifies adversarial training across heterogeneous sampling rates.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The paper demonstrates strong results across a diverse set of tasks (general restoration on UNIVERSE, denoising on VCTK-DEMAND and DNS 2020, multi-rate super-resolution, and real-world audio on VoxCeleb and URGENT 2025), supported by detailed ablations on architecture, loss functions, and rate balance.
weaknesses: Reliance on automated perceptual metrics over human listening tests: Evaluation of perceptual quality relies almost entirely on automated non-intrusive MOS predictors (UTMOS, DNSMOS, NISQA). Given that generative restoration models frequently introduce subtle hallucination artifacts that automated predictors can overestimate, subjective listening tests (e.g., MUSHRA or crowd-sourced MOS) would have provided stronger validation.

Limited diversity in pretraining data: The unified model is trained primarily on VCTK (98 English speakers). While synthetic augmentations are extensive, relying on a single, clean, English-only corpus raises questions regarding real-world cross-lingual generalization, especially given the model's reliance on WavLM features.

Trade-off against specialized fidelity models: In benchmarks emphasizing intrusive waveform fidelity (e.g., URGENT 2025 in Table 12 and DNS 2020 in Table 14), the unified TF-Restormer exhibits a noticeable gap behind specialized discriminative systems in intrusive metrics (PESQ, SI-SDR), highlighting the inherent trade-off of generative restoration under severe degradations.
